course.title: Boot.dev Back-end Developer Path (Python + Go)
course.format: self-paced interactive online track: 16 courses + 8 projects (6 guided, 2 portfolio), in-browser exercises plus local projects
course.audience: beginners aiming for back-end developer roles
course.notes: Course list and order taken from boot.dev/tracks/backend as fetched 2026-10-12 (24 items). Order differs from older versions of the path: Build an AI Agent now comes right after Functional Programming and before DSA; Static Site Generator follows DSA. Courses present in older path versions (e.g. Learn CI/CD, Kubernetes, earlier JavaScript/TypeScript courses) are NOT in the current listing, so no cicd/kubernetes/javascript concepts are included. Topics are the published chapter titles; individual lesson titles are not shown on public course pages, so concept mappings below chapter level are inferred from chapter descriptions and general knowledge of the courses (e.g. regex/unittest/enums in the SSG, match statement in Sum Types, sys.argv in BookBot, binary/bitwise in 'Computing'), and should be treated as moderately confident. The 'Learn Python for Beginners' slug is learn-python-beginners (marketed as Learn to Code in Python). The AI Agent project currently uses free models on OpenRouter via the OpenAI Python SDK (earlier versions used Google Gemini). The SQL course page does not name its engine (believed SQLite in-browser; uncertain). Portfolio projects (Personal Project 1, Capstone) list no public chapters. Python-language concept IDs are reused for analogous Go constructs only where noted via course_label (e.g. enums, modules_imports, pointers). Python-based modules are 1,3,5,6,7,8,9,10; Linux and Git are language-agnostic; Memory Management is C; most later courses are Go.
